# Scenario X02 — Poor Activation but Strong Retained Usage

**Domain:** PLG SaaS. **Situation:** product health, mature.

## Context

A product-led SaaS ("Flow," a project management tool) signs up 8,000 free accounts a month.
Product leadership is worried about activation: the median new account completes its first
project in 9 days, and 55% of new accounts never create a project at all. At the same time,
retained usage is strong: accounts that do reach their third week show a 4-month retention
curve that is above the category benchmark, and NRR on converted accounts is 118%.

The CEO frames the problem as "activation is broken; fix onboarding." One director argues the
real problem is acquisition quality — the marketing team is pulling in accounts that never had
a use case. Another argues the data is fine and the fix is to convert the retained-but-not-paying
middle. A previously run experiment that changed the onboarding checklist did not move
activation.

## Inputs available (imperfect)

- Cohort data by signup source (organic search, paid, partner, referral) exists but has not
  been segmented against the retention curve.
- A survey of new accounts who never created a project exists but was never analyzed.
- No experiment has tested a different signup qualification or a use-case-based onboarding flow.
- Revenue is healthy; no immediate runway pressure.

## Ask

You have one page to recommend what the team should conclude about activation and what to do
next. State your reasoning and the evidence you are relying on or missing.
